read.sections.0.text.note: 'Đa ngôn ngữ' for multilingual (glossary word); some may prefer 'nói được nhiều thứ tiếng'. Language names: tiếng Tây Ban Nha, Guaraní (kept), Somali, Ả Rập, Tamil, 'Mã Lai' for Malay (some use 'Malay'). Please check each. The last two sentences (English skill does not show cleverness) should be checked for kindness and clarity. | Review: 'Nghe một từ mình biết' uses mình generically; 'bạn' may be safer. Also 'kí hiệu' (L11, L07, L16, geography) vs 'ký hiệu' (course.json, culture.json) are inconsistent across files.
read.sections.0.text.source: People use language to share news, jokes, memories and care. Hearing a word you know can help you feel welcome in a new place. Many people in the world are multilingual. In Paraguay, for example, many people speak both Spanish and Guaraní. Someone who speaks Somali, Arabic and English, or Tamil and Malay, can help different groups understand each other. That is a real skill. How well a person speaks English does not show how clever they are. It does not show whether their ideas matter.
read.sections.0.text.back: People use language to share news, jokes, memories and care. Hearing a word you know can help you feel welcomed in a new place. Many people in the world are multilingual, meaning they speak more than one language. For example in Paraguay, many people speak both Spanish and Guaraní. A person who speaks Somali, Arabic and English, or Tamil and Malay, can help different groups of people understand each other. That is a real skill. How well a person speaks English does not show how smart that person is. It also does not show whether their opinion matters or not.

read.sections.0.simpler.source: People use language to share news, jokes and care. A word you know can help you feel welcome. Many people are multilingual. They speak two or more languages. All people's ideas matter.
read.sections.0.simpler.back: People use language to share news, jokes and care. A word you know helps you feel welcomed. Many people are multilingual. They speak two or more languages. In Paraguay, many people speak Spanish and Guaraní. If you can speak two or three languages, you can help other people. That is a real skill. Speaking English well does not show that a person is smart. Everyone's opinion matters.

read.sections.1.text.note: 'Người khiếm thính' for Deaf people (the English capital-D Deaf community). Some Vietnamese Deaf community members prefer 'người điếc'; a native check, ideally with a Deaf reader, is needed. 'Hơn 300 ngôn ngữ kí hiệu' is the UN figure. 'Hình biểu tượng', 'dễ tiếp cận' (accessible), 'phiên dịch' (interpret) are glossary choices.
read.sections.1.text.source: Communication is not only speaking and writing. Deaf communities use sign languages, which are full languages with their own grammar. The United Nations says there are more than 300 sign languages in the world. People also use gestures, pictures and clear design. The pictogram on the notice shows food, a clock, a calendar and a map. This makes the notice more accessible, because more people can understand the main message. But a picture cannot give every detail, such as what to bring. A volunteer who can interpret still helps.
read.sections.1.text.back: Communication is not only speaking and writing. Deaf communities use sign language. These are full languages with their own grammar. The United Nations says the world has more than 300 sign languages. People also use gestures, pictures and clear design. The icons on the notice draw food, a clock, a calendar and a map. Because of that the notice is more accessible, since more people can understand the main message. But a picture cannot say every detail, for example what to bring. A volunteer who can interpret is still very helpful.

read.sections.1.simpler.back: Communication is not only speaking and writing. Deaf people use sign language. These are full languages. There are more than 300 such languages. read.sections.2.heading.back: Languages change and borrow words from each other

read.sections.2.text.note: Examples in other languages are kept as in the English: qahwah, kahveh, caffè, 'coffee'. Note that Vietnamese 'cà phê' itself came from French; the lesson does not mention it, but a reviewer may want a note. Language names: tiếng Thổ Nhĩ Kỳ, tiếng Ý, tiếng Hindi, tiếng Ba Tư (Persian), tiếng Hausa. 'Họ ngôn ngữ' for language family (alternative 'ngữ hệ', more formal). Check the claim about families reads correctly.
read.sections.2.text.source: Languages change over time. They also borrow words from each other when people meet and trade. The English word “coffee” travelled a long way. It started as the Arabic word qahwah. It became kahveh in Turkish and caffè in Italian, and then it reached English. Many languages are also related. English, Hindi and Persian belong to one language family, because they grew from one very old language. Arabic, Somali and Hausa belong to another family. No language is better than another. Each one carries the knowledge and stories of the people who speak it.
read.sections.2.text.back: Languages change over time. They also borrow words from each other when people meet and trade. The English word "coffee" has come a long way. At first it was the Arabic word qahwah. It became kahveh in Turkish and caffè in Italian, and only then came to English. Many languages are also related like relatives. English, Hindi and Persian belong to the same language family, because they all developed from one very ancient language. Arabic, Somali and Hausa belong to another family. No language is better than another. Each language carries the knowledge and stories of the people who speak it.

read.sections.2.simpler.note: 'Giống như anh em họ' for 'like cousins'. Check that the family idea is clear and 'họ ngôn ngữ' is understood.
read.sections.2.simpler.source: Languages change over time. They take words from each other. Look at the word “coffee”. It began in Arabic. Then it went into Turkish and Italian. Then it came into English. Some languages are like cousins. They grew from one old language. So they are in one language family. English, Hindi and Persian are in one. Arabic, Somali and Hausa are in a different one. No language is the best. Each one holds the stories of the people who speak it.
read.sections.2.simpler.back: Languages change over time. They take words from each other. Look at the word "coffee". It started in Arabic. Then it went into Turkish and Italian. Then it came to English. Some languages are like cousins. They grew up together from one old language. So they belong to the same language family. English, Hindi and Persian belong to one family. Arabic, Somali and Hausa belong to another family. No language is the best. Each language keeps the stories of the people who speak it.

watch.summary.source: This animated video explains how languages change. Long ago, groups of people who spoke one language moved apart. They lived in new places and met new neighbours. Over many years, each group changed the way it spoke. New words came in, and sounds changed. In time, one language became several languages. Languages that grew from one older language form a language family. Language experts compare grammar and basic words, like numbers, to find these links. Some words are borrowed from neighbours, so experts check them with care. It can be hard to say where one language ends and another begins. So different experts count between 3,000 and 8,000 languages in the world. The video ends with an idea: a language that sounds new to you may be related to one you know.
watch.summary.back: This animated video explains how language changes. A very long time ago, groups of people who spoke the same language moved far from each other. They lived in new places and met new neighbours. Over many years, each group changed its way of speaking. New words appeared, and sounds changed too. Gradually, one language became many languages. Languages that grew from one older language form a language family. Language experts compare grammar and basic words, like counting numbers, to find this connection. Some words are borrowed from neighbours, so the experts check them very carefully. Sometimes it is hard to say where one language ends and where another begins. Because of this, experts count between 3,000 and 8,000 languages in the world. The video ends with one idea: a language that sounds strange to you may be related to a language you already know.
